title: The purpose behind the wonders of Jesus
source_text: Τί μὲν γὰρ βουλομένη ἡ πρόνοια τὰ περὶ τὸν Ἀριστέαν παράδοξα ἐπραγματεύετο, καὶ τί ὠφελῆσαι τὸ τῶν ἀνθρώπων γένος βουλομένη τὰ τηλικαῦτα, ὡς οἴει, ἐπεδείκνυτο; οὐκ ἔχεις λέγειν. ἡμεῖς δὲ, ἐπὰν τὰ περὶ τοῦ Ἰησοῦ διηγώμεθα, οὐ τὴν τυχοῦσαν φέρομεν ἀπολογίαν περὶ τοῦ ταῦτα γεγονέναι, τὸ τὸν θεὸν βεβουλῆσθαι συστῆσαι τὸν διὰ Ἰησοῦ ὡς σωτήριον τοῖς ἀνθρώποις λόγον. βεβαιούμενον μὲν τοῖς ἀποστόλοις ὡσπερεὶ θεμελίοις τῆς καταβαλλομένης οἰκοδομῆς τοῦ χριστιανισμοῦ ἐπιδιδόντα δὲ καὶ κατὰ τοὺς ἑξῆς χρόνους, ἐν οἷς οὐκ ὀλίγαι θεραπεῖαι τῷ Ἰησοῦ ὀνόματι καὶ ἄλλαι τινὲς ἐπιφάνειαι οὐκ εὐκαταφρόνητοι ἐπιτελοῦνται. ποταπὸς δὲ καὶ ὁ Ἀπόλλων, ἐπισκήπτων Μεταποντίνοις ἐν θεῶν μοίρᾳ νέμειν τὸν Ἀριστέαν; καὶ τί βουλόμενος τοῦτο ποιεῖ, ποίαν τε ὠφέλειαν ἐκ τῆς ὡς πρὸς θεὸν τιμῆς οἰκονομῶν τοῖς Μεταποντίνοις γενέσθαι, εἰ τὸν πρὸ ὀλίγου ἄνθρωπον νῦν θεὸν λογίζοιντο; ἀλλ᾿ Ἀπόλλωνος μὲν, τοῦ καθ᾿ ἡμᾶς δαίμονος λαχόντος γέρας „λοιβῆς τε κνίσσης τε,“ αἱ περὶ τοῦ Ἀριστέου συστάσεις ἀξιόλογοί σοι φαίνονται εἶναι, αἱ δὲ τοῦ ἐπὶ πᾶσι θεοῦ καὶ τῶν ἁγίων ἀγγέλων αὐτοῦ διὰ προφητῶν οὐ μετὰ τὸ γεγονέναι τὸν Ἰησοῦν ἀλλὰ πρὶν ἐπιδημῆσαι τῷ βίῳ τῶν ἀνθρώπων προαγορευόμεναι οὐ κινοῦσί σε πρὸς τὸ θαυμάσαι καὶ τοὺς χωρήσαντας θεῖον πνεῦμα προφήτας καὶ τὸν ὑπ᾿ αὐτῶν προφητευόμενον; οὗ τὴν εἰς τὸν βίον ἐπιδημίαν πολλοῖς πρότερον ἔτεσιν οὕτω διὰ πλειόνων κεκηρύχθαι συμβέβηκεν, ὥστε τὸ Ἰουδαίων ὅλον ἔθνος ἠρτημένον τῆς περὶ τοῦ ἐλπιζομένου ἐπιδημήσειν προσδοκίας εἰς τὴν πρὸς ἀλλήλους ζήτησιν ἐληλυθέναι τοῦ Ἰησοῦ ἐπιδημήσαντος, καὶ πολὺ μὲν πλῆθος αὐτῶν ὡμολογηκέναι Χριστὸν καὶ πεπιστευκέναι αὐτὸν εἶναι τὸν προφητευόμενον τοὺς δὲ μὴ πιστεύοντας, καταφρονήσαντας τῆς πρᾳότητος τῶν διὰ τὰ Ἰησοῦ μαθήματα οὐδὲ μέχρι τοῦ τυχόντος στασιάζειν βουληθέντων, τολμῆσαι κατὰ τοῦ Ἰησοῦ τοιαῦτα, ἅτινα φιλαλήθως καὶ εὐγνωμόνως ἀνέγραψαν οἱ μαθηταὶ αὐτοῦ, οὐχ ὑπεκκλέψαντες τῆς περὶ αὐτοῦ παραδόξου ἱστορίας τὸ δοκοῦν τοῖς πολλοῖς αἰσχύνην τῷ λόγῳ Χριστιανῶν φέρειν. καὶ αὐτὸς γὰρ ὁ Ἰησοῦς ἐβούλετο καὶ οἱ μαθηταὶ αὐτοῦ μὴ μόνον τῇ θειότητι καὶ τοῖς παραδόξοις αὐτοῦ πιστεύειν τοὺς προσιόντας, ὡς οὐ κοινωνήσαντος τῇ ἀνθρωπίνῃ φύσει οὐδ᾿ ἀναλαβόντος τὴν ἐν ἀνθρώποις σάρκα ἐπιθυμοῦσαν „κατὰ τοῦ πνεύματος“· ἀλλὰ γὰρ καὶ τὴν καταβᾶσαν εἰς ἀνθρωπίνην φύσιν καὶ εἰς ἀνθρωπίνας περιστάσεις δύναμιν καὶ ἀναλαβοῦσαν ψυχὴν καὶ σῶμα ἀνθρώπινον ἑώρων ἐκ τοῦ πιστεύεσθαι μετὰ τῶν θειοτέρων συμβαλλομένην εἰς σωτηρίαν τοῖς πιστεύουσιν, ὁρῶσιν ὅτι ἀπ᾿ ἐκείνου ἤρξατο θεία καὶ ἀνθρωπίνη συνυφαίνεσθαι φύσις, ἵν᾿ ἡ ἀνθρωπίνη τῇ πρὸς τὸ θειότερον κοινωνίᾳ γένηται θεία οὐκ ἐν μόνῳ τῷ Ἰησοῦ ἀλλὰ καὶ πᾶσι τοῖς μετὰ τοῦ πιστεύειν ἀναλαμβάνουσι βίον, ὃν Ἰησοῦς ἐδίδαξεν, ἀνάγοντα ἐπὶ τὴν πρὸς θεὸν φιλίαν καὶ τὴν πρὸς ἐκεῖνον κοινωνίαν πάντα τὸν κατὰ τὰς Ἰησοῦ ὑποθήκας ζῶντα.
pass_a_gloss: For wishing (βούλομαι) what did providence (πρόνοια) effect (πραγματεύομαι) the marvels about Aristeas, and wishing to benefit (ὠφελέω) the race of men in what, did it display (ἐπιδείκνυμι) such great things, as you think? You cannot say. But we, when we narrate (διηγέομαι) the things about Jesus, bring no ordinary defence (οὐ τὴν τυχοῦσαν ἀπολογίαν) of their having happened: that God willed to commend/establish (συνίστημι) the word (λόγος) through Jesus as saving (σωτήριος) for men, being confirmed (βεβαιόω) by the apostles as it were foundations (θεμέλιοι) of the building (οἰκοδομή) of Christianity (χριστιανισμός) being laid down (καταβάλλω), and increasing (ἐπιδίδωμι) also in the following times, in which not few healings (θεραπεῖαι) in the name (ὄνομα) of Jesus and certain other manifestations (ἐπιφάνειαι) not easily despised are accomplished (ἐπιτελέω). And of what sort (ποταπός) also is Apollo, enjoining the Metapontines to assign Aristeas in the portion of the gods? And wishing what does he do this, and what benefit arranging (οἰκονομέω) to come to the Metapontines from the honour as to a god, if they should reckon (λογίζομαι) the one a man a little before now a god? But of Apollo — the demon (δαίμων), according to us (καθ' ἡμᾶς), having obtained the privilege (γέρας) 'of libation and savour (λοιβή, κνῖσα)' — the commendations (συστάσεις) about Aristeas appear to you worthy of account (ἀξιόλογοι); but those of the God over all and of his holy angels, foretold (προαγορεύω) through prophets not after Jesus had come into being but before he visited (ἐπιδημέω) the life of men, do not move you to marvel at both the prophets who received (χωρέω) divine spirit (θεῖον πνεῦμα) and the one prophesied by them? Whose visit (ἐπιδημία) into life it happened (συμβαίνω) to have been proclaimed (κηρύσσω) many years before thus through many, so that the whole nation (ἔθνος) of Jews, hung upon (ἀρτάομαι) the expectation (προσδοκία) about the one hoped (ἐλπίζω) to come, came into questioning (ζήτησις) toward one another when Jesus came, and a great multitude of them confessed (ὁμολογέω) Christ and believed him to be the one prophesied, but those not believing, despising (καταφρονέω) the meekness (πρᾳότης) of those who on account of the teachings of Jesus did not wish to stir up faction (στασιάζω) not even to the slightest degree (μέχρι τοῦ τυχόντος), dared (τολμάω) against Jesus such things as his disciples truth-lovingly (φιλαλήθως) and candidly (εὐγνωμόνως) recorded, not secretly removing (ὑπεκκλέπτω) from the marvellous story about him what seems to the many to bring shame (αἰσχύνη) to the word of Christians. For both Jesus himself wished, and his disciples, that those coming (προσιόντες) believe not only in his divinity (θειότης) and his marvels, as not having shared (κοινωνέω) in human nature (φύσις) nor taken up (ἀναλαμβάνω) the flesh (σάρξ) among men desiring 'against the spirit' (ἐπιθυμέω κατὰ τοῦ πνεύματος); but they also saw that the power (δύναμις) which came down (καταβαίνω) into human nature and into human circumstances (περιστάσεις) and took up a human soul (ψυχή) and body, from being believed, contributes (συμβάλλομαι) with the more divine things toward salvation (σωτηρία) for those believing, who see that from him divine and human nature began to be woven together (συνυφαίνω), so that the human by fellowship (κοινωνία) with the more divine might become divine (θεία), not in Jesus alone but also in all who with believing take up the life (βίος) which Jesus taught, leading up (ἀνάγω) to friendship (φιλία) toward God and fellowship with him everyone living according to the precepts (ὑποθῆκαι) of Jesus.
pass_b_english: For what purpose did providence work the marvels about Aristeas, and what benefit did it mean to bring to the human race by displaying things as great as you think these were? You cannot say. But when we tell the story of Jesus, we offer no ordinary defence for these things having happened: namely, that God willed to commend as saving for men the message that came through Jesus. That message was made firm through the apostles, as it were the foundations of the building of Christianity that was being laid (Ephesians 2:20), and it has grown in later times too, in which not a few healings are performed in the name of Jesus, along with certain other manifestations that are not to be despised.

And what sort of being is Apollo, who enjoins the Metapontines to count Aristeas among the gods? With what purpose does he do this, and what benefit is he arranging for the Metapontines from honouring Aristeas as a god, if they should now reckon as a god one who a little before was a man? Yet the commendations of Aristeas by Apollo, who in our view is a demon that has received as his privilege "libation and the savour of sacrifice" (Homer, Iliad 4.49), seem to you worth mention; while the commendations from the God over all and his holy angels, foretold through prophets not after Jesus had come but before he came to dwell in human life, do not move you to marvel both at the prophets who received the divine Spirit and at the one whom they prophesied?

It came about that his coming into this life was proclaimed many years beforehand, and by so many, that the whole nation of the Jews, hanging on the expectation of the one they hoped would come, fell to debating among themselves when Jesus came. A great multitude of them confessed him as Christ and believed that he was the one prophesied. But those who did not believe despised the meekness of those who, because of the teachings of Jesus, would not stir up strife even in the least, and dared to do against Jesus such things as his disciples recorded with love of truth and candour, not stealthily removing from the wonderful story about him what seems to most people to bring shame on the Christians' message.

For both Jesus himself and his disciples wished those who came to them to believe not only in his divinity and his marvels, as if he had not shared in human nature or taken on the flesh which in human beings "desires against the spirit" (Galatians 5:17). But they saw too that the power which came down into human nature and human circumstances, and took on a human soul and body, contributes by being believed, together with the more divine things, to the salvation of those who believe, who see that from him the divine and human natures began to be woven together, so that the human, by fellowship with what is more divine, might become divine, not in Jesus alone but also in all who, along with believing, take up the life which Jesus taught, the life that leads everyone who lives by the precepts of Jesus to friendship with God and fellowship with him.

choices.choice: Galatians 5:17 is quoted ('ἐπιθυμοῦσαν κατὰ τοῦ πνεύματος', from 'ἡ σὰρξ ἐπιθυμεῖ κατὰ τοῦ πνεύματος'). 'spirit' is kept lower case because Origen here sets flesh against spirit within the human being; many translators of Galatians capitalise it as the Holy Spirit. The apostles as 'foundations' of the 'building' is a clear allusion to Ephesians 2:20 ('built on the foundation of the apostles and prophets'), cited inline. βεβαιούμενον ('made firm') may echo Hebrews 2:3-4 or Mark 16:20 (the word confirmed with signs); uncertain, not cited. 'λοιβῆς τε κνίσσης τε' is Homer, Iliad 4.49 (Zeus on the gods' privilege; the line recurs at Iliad 24.70). 'λόγος' in 'τὸν διὰ Ἰησοῦ ... λόγον' and 'τῷ λόγῳ Χριστιανῶν' is the Christian message, not the divine Word, so 'message' in lower case. 'θεῖον πνεῦμα' rendered 'the divine Spirit' (the Spirit who spoke in the prophets). 'πολλοῖς πρότερον ἔτεσιν οὕτω διὰ πλειόνων ... ὥστε' rendered 'many years beforehand, and by so many, that'; διὰ πλειόνων most likely means many prophets, but the noun is not supplied. The 'commendations' (συστάσεις) of the God over all and his angels are, by context, testimonies to Jesus; the reading text does not add his name. The great multitude of Jews who believed may recall Acts 21:20; possible only, not cited. ἀνάγοντα (masc. acc.) agrees with βίον: it is the life that leads its followers to friendship with God. Reviewer: βεβαιούμενον μὲν τοῖς ἀποστόλοις taken as an instrumental dative ('made firm through the apostles'); a present passive rarely takes a dative of agent. ὁρῶσιν agrees with τοῖς πιστεύουσιν, so it is rendered as a relative clause ('who see'), not a new causal sentence.
'Apollo, enjoining the Metapontines' -> 'Apollo, who enjoins the Metapontines' (participle ἐπισκήπτων belongs to Apollo; clearer English)
'fell to disputing' -> 'fell to debating' (ζήτησις is inquiry or debate, not quarrel)
'his wonders' -> 'his marvels' (τοῖς παραδόξοις; same word rendered 'marvels' throughout these chapters)
'They saw also that' -> 'But they saw too that' (restores the contrast of ἀλλὰ γὰρ καί after 'not only')

verified: Galatians 5:17 'ἡ γὰρ σὰρξ ἐπιθυμεῖ κατὰ τοῦ πνεύματος' (quotation, inline); Ephesians 2:20 'built on the foundation of the apostles' (clear allusion, inline); Homer, Iliad 4.49 'λοιβῆς τε κνίσης τε· τὸ γὰρ λάχομεν γέρας ἡμεῖς' matches λαχόντος γέρας; ὁρῶσιν agrees with τοῖς πιστεύουσιν; ἀνάγοντα agrees with βίον; 'might become divine' keeps γένηται θεία exactly
